title: Jonah and the Colony
premise: Gideon Iversen smuggles memories—recorded experiences pressed into data-pearls—past the customs ring of Meridian Station, hiding her own erased past inside the cargo. When a routine job includes a manifest listing a passenger named 'Jonah' aboard the Halcyon, a colony ship that officially never launched, Gideon traces it to Kestrel's Landing, a settlement whose records were purged after a corporate massacre. As she recovers survivors' memory-pearls and rebuilds the truth fragment by fragment, she discovers Jonah is herself: a version of her identity she buried to survive. The corporation's enforcers close in as she broadcasts the recovered memories station-wide, forcing Meridian to choose between comfortable lies and unbearable truth; in the end, Gideon surrenders her anonymity, takes the name Jonah publicly, and founds an archive of the dead with the ragtag crew who became her family.
about_author: Mirabel Ravensworth is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction about the people those systems erase. She writes from a converted cargo pod and claims she can still smell vacuum sealant on every page.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Heart
chapters.summary: Gideon Iversen runs a memory-pearl shipment past Meridian Station customs, hiding contraband grief-recordings inside legitimate freight. Her POV establishes her rules: no names, no attachments, no questions. But a client's pearl she shouldn't have peeked at shows a green field on a colony she's never heard of. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Was
chapters.summary: A fence pays Gideon to authenticate a salvaged ship's black box. The manifest lists the Halcyon, bound for Kestrel's Landing, carrying 412 colonists—including a passenger named Jonah Iversen. Her hands shake: that is nearly her name, and the Halcyon appears in no registry. POV: Gideon. Beat: the first crack in her invisibility.

chapters.title: Customs and Consequence
chapters.summary: Inspector Vey Okafor flags Gideon's last three shipments, suspicious of her perfect record. Meanwhile she queries a records-broker, Dax, who warns that Kestrel's Landing files were purchased and purged by Calloway Biologics. POV alternates Gideon and Okafor, who genuinely wants to be honest in a dishonest system. Beat: hunter and hunted circling.

chapters.title: Green Fields, Dead Air
chapters.summary: Gideon jumps to the coordinates from the black box and finds Kestrel's Landing scorched and abandoned, atmosphere processors failing. In a shelter she finds a cache of memory-pearls labeled like seed stock. Playing one, she hears a child singing—and sees her own face in a reflection within someone else's memory. Beat: dread blooming into obsession.

chapters.title: The Crew You Don't Choose
chapters.summary: Back at Meridian, Gideon reluctantly recruits help: Dax the broker, engineer Sefa who owes her a life-debt, and retired pilot Amara Okonkwo who once flew colony routes and remembers the Halcyon launching—though she was paid to forget. Found family begins forming around shared guilt. Beat: warmth arriving against her will.

chapters.title: Pearls Before Enforcers
chapters.summary: Calloway's private security, led by the courteous, terrifying Mr. Latch, searches Gideon's berth and confiscates her mother-of-all decryption key. She escapes with one pearl hidden in a body implant—the same place her own erased memories were cut out. Beat: violation and resolve; she realizes they know what she is.

chapters.title: What the Child Saw
chapters.summary: The salvaged pearl plays fully: a girl's-eye view of Calloway troops sealing the colony dome while colonists suffocate, recorded by a woman whispering 'Jonah, run.' Gideon recognizes the whisperer's voice as her own. POV shifts into the memory itself, intimate and terrible. Beat: horror fused with self-recognition.

chapters.title: Amara's Confession
chapters.summary: Amara admits she piloted the evacuation shuttle that left 400 behind under corporate orders, then sold her memory of it. She kept only the guilt. Gideon, furious, almost walks away—but stays when Amara reveals the shuttle's flight logs survived in her old union pension file. Beat: forgiveness as a choice, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Erasure Clinic
chapters.summary: Gideon tracks the clinic where her memories were taken, posing as a client. The technician, bribed with a rare pearl, confirms a woman matching her description paid to forget Kestrel's Landing—and left a message for herself: 'If you came back, you already know why.' Beat: grief for a self she can't remember being.

chapters.title: Okafor's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Inspector Okafor finds the purged registry entries half-restored and confronts her superiors, who order her to drop it. She copies the fragments anyway and anonymously sends them to Gideon—crossing her own line. Beat: the system's first defection; hope has a badge now.

chapters.title: Latch Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Mr. Latch offers Gideon a deal: surrender the pearls and he'll reveal what 'Jonah' did at Kestrel's Landing. His hint—that Jonah wasn't a victim but a witness who testified and was silenced—shatters her assumption of innocence. Beat: identity as threat; maybe she ran from complicity, not just trauma.

chapters.title: The Testimony Fragment
chapters.summary: Dax reconstructs a corrupted arbitration recording: Jonah Iversen, colony liaison, testified that Calloway knowingly shipped defective dome seals. The tribunal was bought; Jonah was scheduled for 'memory remediation' and vanished. Gideon realizes she chose erasure to survive the verdict. Beat: reclaiming the name as an act of courage, not shame.

chapters.title: Sefa's Bargain
chapters.summary: To decrypt the full pearl archive, Sefa must cannibalize the crew's own ship systems, stranding them if anything fails. She does it anyway, saying family means betting the boat. Mid-conversion, Latch's team raids the dock; Amara flies them out through unlicensed gates. Beat: sacrifice cementing the found family.

chapters.title: Four Hundred Twelve Names
chapters.summary: The decrypted archive contains every colonist's final recorded day. The crew spends a night listening, grieving strangers, building the list of names. Gideon finally weeps—not for herself but for the people she failed as their advocate. Beat: mourning as the engine of purpose.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Problem
chapters.summary: Truth without distribution dies quietly. The crew plans to hijack Meridian's public memory-lattice during the Founder's Day ceremony, when every resident plugs in. Okafor agrees to look away for exactly eleven minutes. Beat: audacity; the plan is beautiful and probably fatal.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter before the storm: Amara teaches Gideon to fly, Dax gives Gideon his real name, Sefa installs the broadcast rig. Gideon decides that whatever happens, she'll take back 'Jonah' publicly. Beat: tenderness and readiness; the family is real now.

chapters.title: Founder's Day
chapters.summary: The heist begins. Sefa breaches the lattice, Dax spoofs authentication, Okafor stalls her own inspectors. Latch anticipates them—he leaked the ceremony plan as bait—and cuts the uplink. Beat: the trap springs; everything hinges on a backup no one believes exists.

chapters.title: Eleven Minutes
chapters.summary: Amara rams the Halcyon's salvaged black box into the lattice core as a physical relay. The massacre plays across every screen on Meridian: 412 lives ending in real time. Crowds stop mid-celebration. Latch orders his team to fire into the crowd; Okafor arrests him instead, choosing sides aloud. Beat: climax—truth as detonation.

chapters.title: The Verdict of Strangers
chapters.summary: Meridian's citizens, jury by mob and then by tribunal, demand accountability. Calloway's local charter is suspended; the arbitration judge flees. Gideon testifies under her birth name, Jonah Iversen, describing both the testimony she gave and the erasure she bought. Beat: identity reclaimed through public witness.

chapters.title: Latch's Last Offer
chapters.summary: In custody, Latch reveals Calloway's parent company will simply rebrand and return—and offers Gideon a place selling memories again, safely invisible. She refuses: 'I'm done being nobody.' He leaves her with one gift: the clinic's master index, so others can find their stolen years. Beat: temptation declined; mercy extended.

chapters.title: The Archive of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the crew opens a free archive on Kestrel's Landing's rebuilt first deck: every pearl playable, every name read aloud daily. Survivors' relatives arrive from across the system. Gideon/Jonah plants the field from the very first memory-pearl she ever saw. Beat: grief transmuted into institution and home.

chapters.title: Manifest
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Gideon's POV: she amends the Halcyon's manifest, adding the 412 names to the passenger list so history records they flew, lived, and died. Amara, Dax, Sefa, and Okafor sign as crew. Jonah looks at her own name—no longer contraband—and lets the reader understand that memory, kept together, is how the forgotten stay alive. Beat: resolution; found family as living archive.
